newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise in thin early trade.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise in thin early trade.

text.p: French shares rose on Wednesday in thin, pre-holiday trade, buoyed by a "reassuring" message from President Jacques Chirac, who waded into the parliamentary election campaign to support the ruling conservatives.
The bourse was also underpinned by a fresh record close on Wall Street although traders say Wall Street's influence has taken a back seat to political developments in France.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 7.81 points, or 0.31 percent, at 2,660.12 at 0905 GMT. The CAC-40 May futures contract was up 5.5 points at 2,650.5.
Volume was 825 million francs, with activity expected to stay thin ahead of U.S. productivity and trade data due in the afternoon and the Ascension Day holiday in France on Thursday.
Shares in glassmaker Saint-Gobain were up 1.66 percent at 795 francs on a 31 percent jump in first-quarter sales.

Retailer Casino's stock was down but off its lows on news of the departure of management board chairman Georges Plassat, who was viewed as pushing for a merger or alliance for the group. "The stock recovered from its early fall because there's still potential for a merger," a broker said. Casino shares were down 1.63 percent at 271 francs.

Shares in Groupe des Assurances Nationales GAN were up 2.05 percent at 139.40 francs on an article in the newspaper La Tribune saying insurer Assurances Generales de France AGF might make a bid. AGF confirmed that it was interested in GAN's insurance activities.
